interactions.title: Compiler view vs runtime view
interactions.description: Pick a reference type, an object and an action. The left panel is all the compiler knows; the right panel is what actually runs.

interactions.title: Predict the output: what is polymorphic?

questions.explanation: Only instance methods are dispatched on the object's class, so `name()` gives B. Static methods are hidden, not overridden, and fields are never polymorphic: both are chosen by the reference type A.
The compiler only looks at the declared type `Animal`, which has no `fetch()`. The object being a Dog doesn't matter until you downcast.

code.source:
Animal a = new Cat();
Dog d = (Dog) a;

options: Compiles; d refers to the cat
questions.explanation: An `Animal` reference *might* point to a Dog, so the cast compiles. At run time the JVM checks the actual object — a Cat — and throws `ClassCastException`.

interactions.title: Abstract class vs interface (Java 17)
interactions.description: Hide the answers and test your recall — this comparison is asked in almost every Java interview.

cells: Methods are `public` unless `private`; fields are `public static final`
Related classes share state and code (an is-a family)
Unrelated classes share a capability (a can-do contract)
